Philosophy is the systematic, critical study of fundamental questions about existence, [[Knowledge|knowledge]], value, reason, mind and language.

This note maps philosophy as a field. Its properties list every branch, subdomain, historical period, movement, theory, concept and author in this vault. Each of them has its own note, with a short definition, that links back here. Open **Graph View**, or the **Backlinks** panel of any note, to explore the connections.

## How the map is organised

| Property | What it contains | Folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| branch | the main areas of philosophy | Branch |
| subdomain | specialised fields within a branch | Subdomains |
| historical-period | the main periods in the history of philosophy | Historical Periods |
| movements | schools and traditions with a history, such as [[Stoicism]] | Movements |
| theories | positions that can be defended or rejected, such as [[Compatibilism]] | Theories |
| concepts | key ideas and problems, such as [[Justice]] or [[Consciousness]] | Concepts |
| author-links | philosophers | Author |

Some "-isms" are both a historical movement and a position (for example, [[Empiricism]]). In this vault each one appears only once, in the category where it is most often discussed.

## Sources

- Structure: the [PhilPapers taxonomy](https://philpapers.org/browse/all) of philosophy.
- Fuller definitions: the [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu), linked from every note.
- Movements and periods: cross-checked with [Philosophy Basics](https://www.philosophybasics.com/movements).

- Do we have [[Free Will|free will]]?

From the first Greek philosophers to the end of antiquity: the [[Pre-Socratic|Pre-Socratics]], Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, and the Hellenistic and Roman schools, alongside the classical traditions of China and India.

## Sub-periods
- **Pre-Socratic** (7th–5th century BC): the search for the first principle ([[Arche|arche]]) of nature: the [[Milesian School|Milesians]], Heraclitus, Pythagoras, the [[Eleatic School|Eleatics]], the [[Atomism|atomists]].
- **Classical** (5th–4th century BC): the [[Sophism|Sophists]], Socrates, Plato and Aristotle in Athens.
- **Hellenistic** (323–31 BC): schools of the good life: [[Stoicism]], [[Epicureanism]], [[Skepticism|Scepticism]] and [[Cynicism]].
- **Roman and Late Antique** (1st century BC – 5th century AD): Roman Stoicism (Seneca, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius), Cicero, [[Neoplatonism]] (Plotinus).

## Main themes
- What is the first principle of all things?
- Being and change: is reality one and unchanging (Parmenides) or in constant flux (Heraclitus)?
- How should we live, and what is [[Virtue|virtue]]? (Socrates)
- What are the Forms, and how is [[Knowledge|knowledge]] possible? (Plato)
- Substance, causes and purpose in nature (Aristotle)
- How can we reach [[Happiness|happiness]] and tranquillity of mind?

Philosophy in the Christian, Byzantine, Islamic and Jewish worlds, centred on the relationship between [[Faith and Reason|faith and reason]].

- **Early Middle Ages** (6th–10th century): Boethius, Byzantine thought, the preservation of Greek and Latin learning.
- **High Middle Ages** (11th–13th century): the rise of universities and [[Scholasticism]], the recovery of Aristotle through Islamic and Jewish philosophers (Avicenna, Averroes, Maimonides), Anselm, Abelard and Aquinas.

- How do faith and reason relate?
- Can the existence of [[God]] be proved?
- The problem of [[Universals|universals]]: realism or nominalism?
- [[Essence and Existence|Essence and existence]]
- Why does evil exist if God is good, and are we free?
- [[Natural Law Theory|Natural law]] as the basis of morality and politics

Philosophy from the early 20th century to the present, including the analytic and continental traditions.

## Sub-periods
- **Early 20th century** (1900–1930s): the birth of [[Analytic Philosophy|analytic philosophy]] (Frege, Russell, Moore, early Wittgenstein), [[Phenomenology|phenomenology]] (Husserl, Heidegger) and [[Logical Positivism|logical positivism]].
- **Mid 20th century** (1940s–1960s): [[Existentialism|existentialism]] (Sartre, Camus, Beauvoir), [[Ordinary Language Philosophy|ordinary language philosophy]], [[Critical Theory|critical theory]], [[Structuralism|structuralism]], Popper and Kuhn on science.
- **Late 20th century to present** (1970s–today): [[Post-Structuralism|post-structuralism]] (Foucault, Derrida), [[Political Philosophy|political philosophy]] after Rawls, [[Philosophy of Mind|philosophy of mind]] and cognitive science, [[Applied Ethics|applied ethics]], and the [[Ethics of Technology|ethics of technology]] and [[Artificial Intelligence (AI)|AI]].

## Main themes
- Language, meaning and [[Logic|logic]]
- Science, its methods and its limits
- [[Consciousness]] and the [[Mind & Body|mind-body problem]]
- Existence, [[Freedom|freedom]] and [[Authenticity|authenticity]]
- [[Justice]], [[Rights|rights]] and [[Equality|equality]]
- Power, [[Knowledge|knowledge]] and society
- Technology, artificial intelligence and human agency

From Descartes to Nietzsche: [[Rationalism|rationalism]] and [[Empiricism|empiricism]], the [[Enlightenment]], Kant, [[German Idealism|German idealism]], and the great 19th-century systems and their critics.

## Sub-periods
- **Age of Reason** (17th century): the search for certain foundations of [[Knowledge|knowledge]]: Descartes, Hobbes, Spinoza, Leibniz, Locke.
- **Enlightenment** (18th century): reason, science and [[Rights|rights]]: Berkeley, Hume, Voltaire, Rousseau, Smith and Kant.
- **19th century** (1800–1900): German idealism (Hegel), [[Utilitarianism|utilitarianism]] (Bentham, Mill), [[Positivism|positivism]] (Comte), Marx, Kierkegaard, Schopenhauer and Nietzsche.

- [[Certainty]] and the foundations of knowledge
- Reason or experience as the source of knowledge
- The relation between [[Mind & Body|mind and body]]
- The [[Social Contract Theory|social contract]] and the [[Legitimacy|legitimacy]] of the state
- The limits of reason (Kant)
- History, [[Dialectic|dialectic]] and progress
- The critique of religion and traditional morality
